evidence.curator_note: Equation 4.30 (ring decomposition needs TWO ring-bond cleavages to expel a fragment). The full equation draws a three-arrow sequence: (i) cyclohexane loses an electron (-e-) to the C6H12 molecular ion m/z 84, drawn as an intact hexagon with a delocalised '+.', NO arcs; (ii) a sigma ring-bond cleavage isomerises the molecular ion WITHOUT mass change to a ring-opened DISTONIC radical cation, m/z 84 (radical at one chain terminus, charge at the other), NO arcs drawn; (iii) an alpha cleavage at the radical terminus expels neutral ethylene and gives the C4H8 distonic radical cation at m/z 56. THIS RECORD encodes step (iii), the only step the book draws electron arrows for. Structures (i) and (ii) at m/z 84 are drawn but NOT separately encoded: the intact-ring radical cation is a sigma (2-centre-1-electron) radical cation that cannot be localised in a single Kekule SMILES (all ring carbons are 4-coordinate, leaving no room for a localised radical or a 3-coordinate carbenium) -- which is exactly why the book draws it delocalised. The distonic ion m/z 84 IS localisable and is used here as the precursor of the drawn alpha cleavage; it has the same formula/mass (C6H12+., 84.0934) as the molecular ion, so ms_context.precursor_mz = 84.0934 holds for either. ARCS: the book draws THREE fishhook (single-barbed) arcs on structure 3, and ALL THREE encoded moves are drawn -- move <1> the radical-terminus carbon's odd electron -> the forming C1=C2 pi bond [rightmost fishhook, springing from the '.' dot]; move <2> one electron of the C2-C3 sigma bond -> that same forming C1=C2 pi bond [large arc over the ring peak]; move <3> the other electron of the C2-C3 sigma bond -> C3, the new radical site [leftmost fishhook]. This is a complete radical-site alpha-cleavage; NO implicit homolysis hook is required (nothing is left undrawn). The text just below the equation confirms move <1>: 'The unpaired electron in this isomeric ion is donated to form a new bond to the adjacent carbon atom.'

rule_index by_equation cross-links equation 4.30 to a single MOD rule, IMS_4_30 (rule_name 'Ring spaltung generell 4.30'), DFS [C.]1[C]2[C]3[C+]4[C]5{=}[C]6>>[C.]1[C+]2.[C]3{=}[C]4[C]5{=}[C]6. VERIFIED MISMATCH (RDKit-checked) -- IMS_4_30 does NOT reproduce this scheme. (a) Its reactant is C6H10+. -- UNSATURATED, with a pre-existing C5=C6 double bond and an INTERNAL carbenium at C4 -- whereas the book's structure 3 is the SATURATED distonic ion C6H12+. with a TERMINAL carbenium; the formulae differ by H2 (82 vs 84 u). (b) It cleaves C2-C3 to form a NEW C3=C4 double bond and splits into a CHARGED 2-carbon fragment (C1.-C2+, i.e. C2H4+.) plus NEUTRAL butadiene (C4H6). The book's alpha cleavage instead forms the C1=C2 pi bond, expels the two carbons at the radical terminus as NEUTRAL ethylene (C2H4), and RETAINS the charge on the 4-carbon fragment as the m/z 56 radical cation (C4H8+.). So relative to the book the charge ends up on the OTHER fragment and the neutral loss differs (butadiene vs ethylene). IMS_4_30 is mis-encoded relative to book Eq 4.30 (listed in rule_mismatches); no MOD rule faithfully encodes the drawn alpha cleavage. support_type is 'curator_inferred' (NOT 'computationally_supported') precisely because the cross-linked rule does not reproduce the mechanism.

The book labels the fragment ion at nominal m/z 56 directly under structure 4 of Equation 4.30, but prints NO intensity percentage for it on this page (the Unknown 4.11 table and spectrum above belong to an UNRELATED C8H18O molecule, not cyclohexane), so relative_intensity is omitted rather than invented. observed_mz 56.0621 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of the C4H8+. distonic radical cation (electron-mass corrected); the figure shows only the nominal integer 56.
